# Affiliate Marketing for Small Businesses: How to Start Right

Not every small business is a fit for affiliate marketing. Here’s how to know if you are, and a 9-step guide to starting your own program.

13 min read · By [Irene Lopez](https://referralrock.com/about/irene-lopez/) · Reviewed by [Jessica Huhn](https://referralrock.com/about/jessica-huhn/) · Updated July 10, 2026

[How we write and review our articles](https://referralrock.com/about/editorial-standards/)

[Add us as a preferred source](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=referralrock.com)

![affiliate marketing for small businesses. affiliate programs for small businesses](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/x9q04aql/production/bb9b58877738871beec4192672fc4f355ea309f6-900x600.jpg?w=420&auto=format)

## Key takeaways

*   Affiliate marketing works best when you have products with wide appeal and margins that can support ongoing commissions. If you don't, a customer referral program is likely a better fit.
*   Skip affiliate networks — they own your data and relationships, charge steep fees, and put your small business in direct competition with bigger brands for the best affiliates.
*   The best affiliates are partners, not promoters. Consistent communication, clear agreements, and ongoing engagement separate programs that compound over time from ones that fizzle out.

Affiliate marketing has an obvious appeal for small businesses: you pay only when affiliates drive a sale, they bring their own audiences, and your reach multiplies without a big upfront budget. But it doesn’t work for every small business. Before you recruit a single affiliate, there are things you need to have in place — and if you don’t, a customer referral program will serve you better. This guide covers what affiliate marketing actually is, how to tell if it’s the right fit for your business, and 9 steps for starting a program without getting burned by affiliate networks.

## What are affiliate marketing programs?[](https://referralrock.com/affiliate/affiliate-marketing-for-small-business/#what-are-affiliate-marketing-programs)

Affiliate marketing programs involve a brand recruiting content creators and entrepreneurs (“affiliates”) to promote its brand, products, or services. Affiliates can be influencers, bloggers or vloggers, or well-known creatives and personalities who have an established base of loyal, engaged followers. Think of a food blogger promoting their favorite pots and pans as an example.

![Greenpan affiliate program](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/x9q04aql/production/a7fd5ec8d99d209ff37ba6d903cb1984329a0663-1158x696.png?w=900&auto=format)

Source: Greenpan

Affiliates share [trackable affiliate links](https://referralrock.com/affiliate/how-to-create-affiliate-links/) to the brand’s website on their blog and social media posts, websites, newsletters, or other marketing channels. In many cases, the affiliate also creates promotional content for the brand — a blog post, video, or product review, for example — and includes those links for the viewer to get further information or buy the product. This both drives sales for the business, and creates brand awareness among a larger audience — at a lower cost.

The affiliate, in turn, gets commission every time someone makes a purchase through their affiliate link. This allows them to earn passive income while they drive traffic, generate leads, and increase sales for your small business.

## Is affiliate marketing right for your small business?[](https://referralrock.com/affiliate/affiliate-marketing-for-small-business/#is-affiliate-marketing-right-for-your-small-business)

Even though affiliate programs are a great marketing tool for many small online businesses, keep the following criteria in mind before you decide to launch your own affiliate marketing campaign:

*   **Do you know your profit margins?** Your profit margins determine how much you can spend on affiliate commissions. At the end of the day, most affiliates will only promote your brand for the right incentive.
*   **Are you ready to pay commission on every affiliate-driven sale?** If your business is relatively new, you may not be ready to pay affiliate commission for every sale. Or, you may not be able to offer a commission that’s attractive enough for best-fit affiliates. In these cases, it may be best to launch a [customer referral program](https://referralrock.com/program-types/customer-referral/) instead, where you can offer store credit, discount coupons, or other rewards to your best customers.
*   **Does your product have mass appeal?** Affiliates promote your brand to a wide range of people. If your product doesn’t have a wide enough appeal to hook a large target audience, you may not get the full value of an affiliate program.
*   **Do you sell physical products?** Physical products are generally easier for affiliates to promote, particularly on more visual mediums like Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. So, affiliate marketing works best if you’re in an ecommerce or digital product space. If you sell services, you can still [find affiliates](https://referralrock.com/affiliate/how-to-find-affiliates/), but they might target a more niche audience — and you may have to work harder to have them demonstrate your offering.
*   **Do you have access to good-fit affiliates?** Are there content creators who you can easily access _and_ who have audiences that match your own target audience? More popular creators may not be within reach of smaller businesses because they demand higher commissions and brand recognition. In the earlier stages of your business, finding the right content creator to work with your brand may prove difficult.

### Why some small businesses are better off with a referral program[](https://referralrock.com/affiliate/affiliate-marketing-for-small-business/#why-some-small-businesses-are-better-off-with-a-referral-program)

Before deciding between these two options, it helps to understand what makes them fundamentally different.

Affiliate programs are partnerships with content creators and experts. These authorities promote your brand to their own audiences in exchange for a commission. You’re essentially paying for reach. The relationship is between you and an external partner who may never have been your customer.

[Customer referral programs](https://referralrock.com/program-types/customer-referral/) work differently. They tap the customers you already have — the people who’ve used your product or service and would genuinely recommend you to someone they know. # Beginner’s Guide to Affiliate Marketing and How to Start

*   [Business](https://www.wgu.edu/blog/business.html)

![](/content/dam/wgu-65-assets/web-sites/blog-newsroom/blog/images/national/2024/noelle-graf-headshot.jpg)

By [Noelle Graf, Senior Copywriter](https://www.wgu.edu/blog/authors/noelle-graf.html)

Published: Sep 30, 2025

Affiliate marketing is one of the most impactful and cost-effective [digital marketing](https://www.wgu.edu/career-guide/business/digital-marketer-career.html) strategies used by businesses today. This type of marketing involves hiring individuals, known as affiliates, to promote products or services through unique affiliate links in exchange for earning a commission when their referral makes a purchase. It’s a win-win strategy—affiliates earn money while helping businesses boost brand awareness and sales with minimal investment.  

And there has never been a better time to dive in. For those just getting started, this step-by-step affiliate marketing guide provides essential steps and practical tips on how to be an affiliate marketer.  

## What Is Affiliate Marketing?  

Affiliate marketing is a performance-based strategy where either a business or individual, known as an affiliate, earns a commission through marketing another business's goods or services. The affiliate typically earns a percentage of the profit from each sale they make, tracked via affiliate links from one website to another. Influencer marketing is one of the most familiar forms of affiliate marketing, where individuals who have a large social media following are paid by brands to promote their products.  

## What Are the Benefits of Affiliate Marketing?   

Affiliate marketing offers advantages for both businesses and affiliates. Businesses benefit from wider reach and increased sales without taking on much risk, while affiliates—especially those with high follower counts and strong engagement—have the opportunity to earn commissions, make money online, and grow income through platforms they already use.  

Some common benefits of affiliate marketing include:   

**Low cost and low risk.** Becoming an affiliate marketer requires little to no upfront investment. Affiliates act as brand promoters, sharing products or services with their audience in exchange for a commission when their referrals result in sales, leads, or other predefined actions. 

**Easy to scale.** Once an affiliate partnership is established, scaling your audience and influence becomes easier with a strategic content plan. For example, an affiliate who promotes cookware could naturally extend their influence to complementary products such as cooking utensils, linens, and more.   

**Passive income.** After setting up affiliate links or ads on a website, blog, newsletter, or social media platform, affiliates can enjoy the benefits of passive income. Each time a follower clicks through a link, the affiliate earns a commission. 

**Convenient and flexible.** One of the biggest benefits of affiliate marketing is flexibility. Affiliates aren’t tied to a desk or a fixed schedule and can work remotely while building a business that fits their lifestyle.   

## How Does Affiliate Marketing Work?  

The process behind affiliate marketing is straightforward. An affiliate shares an ad or link on their platform of choice, such as a website or social media channel. When a customer clicks on the ad or link, to make a purchase for example, the conversion is tracked, and the affiliate is paid a commission. While commission percentages and payment structures vary depending on the brand and industry, the affiliate is generally rewarded for the sale.  

## How Much Money Can I Make as an Affiliate Marketer?  

A huge incentive for affiliate marketing is that there’s no limit on income. If you have high online engagement and consistently promote your partnerships, you can bring in a substantial amount of money. According to PayScale, the average annual income for affiliate marketers is [$56,141](https://www.payscale.com/research/US/Job=Affiliate_Marketer/Salary) in 2025, with the top 10% earning around $77,000 and the bottom 10% earning $41,000. Industries like fashion and lifestyle are highly competitive, and affiliates with larger followings tend to see greater returns. 

## How Do Affiliate Marketers Get Paid?  

There are a variety of ways affiliate marketers can earn commission, depending on the product or service being promoted. Most affiliates build an income through a mix of the following payment structures:  

**Pay per sale.** This is the most common structure for affiliates, where they earn a percentage from each sale generated through a specific link. For example, a beauty blogger promoting a new skincare line would receive a commission for every purchase made through their blog or social media referral to the company’s website.   

**Pay per action.** In this more complex model, affiliates are compensated when customers take a specific action—such as subscribing to a newsletter or filling out a contact form—after clicking the link. The challenge here is being persuasive enough to encourage a follower or reader to engage directly with the company, leading to notable conversions. 

**Pay per install.** Affiliates earn commissions when users install an app or software via their referral link. For example, an affiliate could make $.10 for every install of a brand’s new app in the first 90 days after its launch. 

**Pay per lead.** Since it’s often easier to generate a lead than a sale, this pay structure is great for beginners who are still building a following. In this case, an affiliate gets paid a commission every time a customer signs up for something, like a sweepstake, a free trial, or an online class. 

**Pay per click.** In this least common compensation model, affiliates earn a commission for every click on their unique link, regardless of whether a purchase or sign-up occurs. Large retailers and corporations often use this structure to build brand awareness and website traffic.

Want to grow your [small and medium business (SMB)](https://www.salesforce.com/ap/small-business/what-is-an-smb/) without breaking the bank? Affiliate marketing could be your secret weapon. By partnering with trusted affiliates — bloggers, influencers, and businesses — you can expand your reach and only pay for actual results. [81% of SMBs say customer referrals and affiliate marketing have helped them grow](https://www.salesforce.com/resources/research-reports/smb-trends/#downloadreporthttps://www.salesforce.com/resources/research-reports/smb-trends/#downloadreport), making it a proven way to boost sales and build brand loyalty​.

But running an affiliate program takes more than just signing up partners. The right strategy, AI-powered tools, and a [customer relationship management (CRM) system](https://www.salesforce.com/crm/what-is-crm/) can help simplify tasks like tracking performance, managing partnerships, and personalizing offers. [Artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.salesforce.com/in/artificial-intelligence/) can analyze which affiliates bring in the most valuable customers, suggest commission adjustments, and improve targeting. In this guide, we’ll cover practical affiliate marketing tips for SMBs and startups.

## What is affiliate marketing for growing your business?

[Affiliate marketing](https://www.salesforce.com/in/blog/affiliate-marketing/) is a low-risk way for SMBs like yours to increase [sales](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/sales/) without a large upfront investment. Instead of running expensive ads, you work with affiliates — partners who promote your products and earn a commission for each sale they bring in. This allows you to expand your reach while keeping costs tied to actual results.

Every affiliate program includes:

*   **Your business (advertiser):** The company offering the product or service.
*   **Affiliates (partners, influencers, and publishers):** Individuals or businesses that promote your brand.
*   **Affiliate networks (optional):** Platforms that track referrals and handle commission payouts.

Affiliate marketing helps your small business increase visibility, attract [loyal customers](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/service/), and [manage marketing costs](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/marketing/) more efficiently. Since you’re only paying for completed [sales](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/), it’s a sustainable strategy that grows with your business.

Your success depends on choosing affiliates who truly connect with your audience. Look for partners who create relevant content, have a loyal following that trusts their recommendations, and use platforms where your customers already spend their time. When trust and alignment come together, your affiliate partnerships become much more effective.

## Affiliate partnership tips: Building strong relationships

Strong affiliate relationships take more than a commission structure — they require trust, [communication](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/collaboration/), and the right support. When your partners feel valued, they’re more likely to create high-quality promotions that bring in the right customers. Here’s how you can set your affiliates up for success.

### Keep communication open and clear

Affiliates are an extension of your business. To ensure they represent your brand accurately, provide clear guidelines, [marketing assets](https://www.salesforce.com/marketing), and regular updates. Using [Slack](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/collaboration/) for real-time communication makes it easier for small businesses to answer questions, share promotions, and strengthen relationships.

### Give affiliates the right marketing tools

Affiliates perform better when they have access to ready-to-use content, promotional banners, and personalized links. An [AI CRM](https://www.salesforce.com/crm/ai-crm/) can help you track which materials work best and tailor future resources to maximize results.

### Use AI to optimize affiliate relationships

AI capabilities like [Agentforce](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/) simplify affiliate management by highlighting top affiliates, and recommending effective commission structures. Instead of manually tracking results, you can use [AI-powered insights](https://www.salesforce.com/in/artificial-intelligence/ai-software-development/) to reward top performers and adjust incentives.

With [Pro Suite](https://www.salesforce.com/small-business/pro-suite/), you can automate performance tracking and use AI-driven recommendations to optimize your affiliate program. By using AI, you create a smarter, more efficient system that benefits both your business and your partners.

# 5 ways small businesses can use affiliate marketing to increase sales

Adam Enfroy

Updated: Jul 21, 2024 · 8 min read

Toolkit for download in this article

Tipsheet: how to ask for referrals

![affiliate marketing, what is affiliate marketing](https://assets.keap.com/image/upload/w_569,h_395,c_limit,q_95,dpr_1/v1530818327/remote_employee_sjmipu.webp)

* * *

As a small business, you need quick and recurring sales to avoid tanking.

Small businesses require loyal customers, but also an influx of new customers to help scale sales.

But, breaking out from the small business startup phase isn’t easy.

Most businesses fail to do it.

Tipsheet: how to ask for referrals

Thankfully, affiliate marketing is taking off right now and is a proven way to increase your sales and brand reach.

Affiliate programs account for [15 to 30% of online sales](https://store.businessinsider.com/products/ultimate-digital-media-reports-bundle-all-reports?IR=T#!/THE-AFFILIATE-MARKETING-REPORT/p/56467038/category=11987293).

In 2017, over [five billion dollars](https://www.pepperjam.com/blog/forrester-report-affiliate-marketing) was spent on affiliate marketing.

Why? It’s a winning strategy for building your brand and expanding your sales.

Just think about it for a minute …

Current trends show that approximately 80% of clients are [seeking out professional services online](https://www.lyfemarketing.com/professional-services-marketing/) when searching.

Can you imagine how much more powerful it is when prospective customers find user-generated content and real humans promoting and marketing your products or services for you?

Here are 5 ways you can leverage affiliate marketing to grow your sales and small business.

### 1\. Utilize user-generated content to expand reach

One of the biggest benefits of affiliate marketing is the expanded reach you can achieve with it.

For example, if you have 20 affiliates in your program, each promoting your products and services, that’s a huge expansion in reach.

If each of those affiliate members has 10,000 followers, that’s a ton of impressions that you would have had to pay to get without affiliate marketing.

And that many impressions don’t come cheap today.

One of the best ways to leverage affiliate marketing as a small business is to promote and encourage user-generated content.

What is that?

Essentially, user-generated content is natural content that promotes your brand but is created by people outside of your brand.

For example, [Buffer](https://buffer.com/) takes advantage of this on Instagram, showcasing Buffer affiliates promoting the hashtag:

![](https://assets.keap.com/image/upload/c_scale,w_600/v1563809830/affiliate%20marketing/Screen_Shot_2019-07-22_at_8.36.58_AM.png)

Check out this other example from [Eterneva](https://www.eterneva.com/blog/eterneva-reviews) on how to repurpose user-generated content into blog posts by sharing customer stories, review videos, and reviews from Google and social media for killer social proof:

![](https://assets.keap.com/image/upload/c_scale,w_600/v1563809901/affiliate%20marketing/Screen_Shot_2019-07-22_at_8.38.11_AM.png)

And it works because 92% of consumers turn to influencers or people they know for product and service referrals.

Social media is the perfect place to showcase user-generated content. Nearly [75% of consumers](https://www.socialmediatoday.com/marketing/masroor/2015-05-28/social-media-biggest-influencer-buying-decisions) depend on social for product/service inspiration.

Within your affiliate program, start encouraging user-generated content.

Develop a game-plan/social scheduling plan to help them improve their own engagement.

Re-share their social posts on your company feed to further promote them.

Consumers are unlikely to believe you when you state that your brand is the best. But if your affiliates are promoting it, they surely will.

### 2\. Leverage affiliate marketing as instant social proof

Just like user-generated content, having affiliates can serve as an instant form of social proof.

In modern times, social proof is everything when it comes to a business.

You need positive reviews. You need word of mouth marketing. You need people outside of your employees to advocate for you.

About [91% of 18-34-year-olds](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) trust reviews as much as personal recommendations!

Affiliates are the perfect candidates to leverage for social proof in two ways:

To give positive reviews of your product or serviceTo give positive reviews for your affiliate program to keep it growing

The benefit here is two-fold.

First, you can interview some of your top affiliates and showcase social proof [right on your website](https://www.housecallpro.com/industries/plumbing-software/):

![](https://assets.keap.com/image/upload/c_scale,w_600/v1563809928/affiliate%20marketing/Screen_Shot_2019-07-22_at_8.38.38_AM.png)

Example: Housecall Pro

This kind of social proof is perfect to serve as a testimonial to attract new customers.

Secondly, on your affiliate signup pages, you will also want to leverage social proof. This can help you attract more top affiliates that will, in turn, expand your audience and boost your sales.

Here is a fantastic example from [Drift](https://www.drift.com/partners/), who uses direct numbers and data to showcase why others should join the program too:

![](https://assets.keap.com/image/upload/c_scale,w_600/v1563809960/affiliate%20marketing/Screen_Shot_2019-07-22_at_8.39.09_AM.png)

With concrete details on how effective your affiliate program is, it will be a no-brainer for others to join.

### 3\. Reward your top affiliates

Let’s be real here…

Affiliate marketers tend to seek out the [top paying affiliate programs](https://www.adamenfroy.com/best-high-paying-affiliate-programs) when searching for brands to partner with and promote.

For someone of the flip side, you’re probably offering a percentage for each sale that is brought in.

The most common is 10%, but some programs can offer more or less based on the products or services being sold:

![](https://assets.keap.com/c_limit,h_100,w_600/v1563809986/affiliate%20marketing/Screen_Shot_2019-07-22_at_8.39.32_AM.png)

Generally speaking, 10% is a great starting point for your affiliate program. It’s enough to attract good affiliates without cutting too far into your profit margins.

But, there is a catch-22:

Users in your affiliate program aren’t going to stick around for long if the
